title: Roosevelt Station

description.main: Photographs of commuters in the Jackson Heights-Roosevelt Avenue subway station in Queens, winner of the first PHOTO 2021 x Perimeter International Photobook Prize.
description.extended:
Roosevelt Station is David Rothenberg's photobook of commuters in the Jackson Heights-Roosevelt Avenue/74th Street subway station in Queens, made in 2019 and 2020 and published by Perimeter Editions in Melbourne in 2021.

The photographs catch commuters, airport-bound travelers, panhandlers and missionaries in the colored light of the station concourse, which comes from Tom Patti's 2004 glass installation Night Passage in the main glass wall. David Campany's essay describes photographing such a space as a mix of reportage and theatre. The 104-page softcover, section-sewn, was the first winner of the PHOTO 2021 x Perimeter International Photobook Prize, chosen from more than 130 entries by a jury that included Michael Mack.

Rothenberg is a photographer and educator living in Queens. His earlier books with ROMAN NVMERALS include Landing Lights Park, which TIME named one of the best photography books of 2018. The publisher places Roosevelt Station in a line with Walker Evans's subway portraits.

notes: Same photographer as row 990 (Landing Lights Park): davidrothenberg.com lists both books and Perimeter's bio cites Landing Lights Park.
